milestone_description: Migrate Java Pet Store 1.3.1_02 to Spring Boot 4.1.1 / Java 21 with MongoDB. 3.5 days.

labels.name: epic
labels.description: Parent issue grouping a work stream

labels.name: risk
labels.description: Carries a named risk from the register

labels.name: cut-candidate
labels.description: Dropped first if the schedule slips

epics.title: Foundation + walking skeleton
epics.summary: Everything that must exist before the real slice is built: the Spring Boot 4.1.1 / Java 21 skeleton, module layout, local infra and CI gates (1.1-1.6), then a tracer bullet through every layer of the target stack on the thinnest possible path (1.7-1.10). Anything the tracer bullet hard-codes, E4 replaces. See docs/adr/0001-target-runtime.md and docs/adr/0006-deliverable-scope-kitchensink-slice.md.

subs.title: 1.1 Skeleton spike: Boot 4.1.1 + Java 21 (web, security, thymeleaf, data-mongodb, events)
subs.acceptance: App boots, one page renders, one document round-trips. TIMEBOX 90 min; on overrun fall back to the latest 3.5.x line and amend ADR-0001.

subs.title: 1.2 Package layout per bounded context + ArchUnit skeleton
subs.acceptance: catalog, cart, customer, order, opc, supplier, admin packages exist; ArchUnit asserts the dependency rules before there is code to violate them.

subs.title: 1.3 compose.yaml (MongoDB, optional Postgres) + run scripts
subs.acceptance: docker compose up then mvn spring-boot:run works from a clean clone.

subs.title: 1.4 GitHub Actions: build, test, ArchUnit, JaCoCo, parity job
subs.acceptance: Checks required on main; parity tests run as their own job so a parity break looks different from a unit-test break.

subs.title: 1.5 Config profiles mongo/jpa, externalised config, Actuator health
subs.acceptance: --spring.profiles.active=jpa switches the store with no code change.

subs.title: 1.6 Repo hygiene: labels, milestone, PR template, branch protection
subs.acceptance: Backlog script runs clean; main is protected; conventional commits documented.

subs.title: 1.7 Walking skeleton: customer registration aggregate, Mongo round-trip
subs.legacy_anchor: components/customer CustomerEJB -> AccountEJB -> ContactInfoEJB -> AddressEJB CMP graph
subs.acceptance: Thinnest possible aggregate (account + contact info only; no profile, no credit card): register, read back from MongoDB, assert the document shape. The domain type carries no Spring Data annotation, so the port/adapter split of 7.1 is proven here rather than asserted later.

subs.title: 1.8 Walking skeleton: Jakarta Validation + Spring Security chain + BCrypt
subs.acceptance: Constraint violations render on the form instead of 500ing; one protected URL redirects when anonymous; passwords are BCrypt from the first commit that stores one, so no plaintext credential path ever exists in this repository's history. Absorbs what was E4.3.

subs.title: 1.9 Walking skeleton: one Thymeleaf form + list page and one REST endpoint
subs.legacy_anchor: signon createuser.jsp + WAF HTMLAction/screenflow; the REST endpoint has NO legacy anchor -- Pet Store predates REST
subs.acceptance: Register-and-list works in a browser and over /api, both through the same application service, proving the view layer is not load-bearing. The missing anchor is the point: first written evidence of a capability the legacy app never had.

subs.title: 1.10 Walking skeleton: test harness proven end to end (Testcontainers, ArchUnit, CI)
subs.legacy_anchor: none -- the legacy codebase ships zero tests, which is itself the finding
subs.acceptance: One Testcontainers-backed integration test over the slice and one ArchUnit rule, green in GitHub Actions on a clean runner. Gate for Epics 3-6: no further slice starts until a slice-shaped test can fail for the right reason.

epics.title: Parity harness: characterization tests + seed data
epics.summary: Encode legacy behaviour as executable tests BEFORE porting it. This is the only defensible definition of functional equivalence, and it is what makes the method scale to a larger codebase.

subs.title: 2.1 Extract catalog seed data to fixtures + loader
subs.acceptance: Same category/product/item counts per locale as the legacy seed; one command reloads.

subs.title: 2.2 Encode the in-scope business rules as parity tests, tagged @Tag("parity")
subs.acceptance: Duplicate-account rejection, sign-on success/failure semantics, locale-scoped catalog rows and the BCrypt deviation each have a test naming the legacy rule or file:line it preserves. The five deferred rules (approval threshold, order-id prefix counter, empty-cart, partial shipment, order lifecycle) are listed as explicitly NOT covered in the traceability matrix - a known gap is not the same as an oversight.

subs.title: 2.3 Legacy -> new traceability matrix
subs.acceptance: Every in-scope legacy component maps to a new component or to an explicit 'dropped, because...'.

subs.title: 2.4 ArchUnit rule set
subs.acceptance: No cross-module internals; no controller -> repository; domain imports no Spring persistence annotation. Violations fail the build.

subs.title: 2.5 Testcontainers base test + CI wiring
subs.acceptance: Mongo-backed tests run in CI with no local install.

epics.title: Catalog slice (read path)
epics.summary: First vertical slice: seeded data to a rendered product page. Proves the whole stack end to end on day 1.

subs.title: 3.1 Domain: Category/Product/Item + locale-scoped details
subs.acceptance: Plain Java, no persistence annotations.

subs.title: 3.2 CatalogRepository port + MongoDB adapter
subs.acceptance: Product page is one findById; the six-way join is gone.

subs.title: 3.3 JPA/H2 adapter for the same port
subs.acceptance: Same port test suite passes under the jpa profile.

subs.title: 3.4 CatalogService: browse, search, paging
subs.acceptance: Search behaviour documented where a text index differs from the legacy LIKE.

subs.title: 3.5 Thymeleaf layout + 4 catalog screens
subs.acceptance: banner/sidebar/body/footer composition preserved.

subs.title: 3.6 REST /api/catalog/**
subs.acceptance: Same application service, no view coupling. Proves the layering.

epics.title: Identity, customer, i18n
epics.summary: Sign-on, account creation and profile taken from the walking-skeleton stub (1.7-1.9) to full parity. Estimates assume the aggregate, the security chain and the registration form already exist; this epic widens them rather than starting them.

subs.title: 4.1 Widen the customer aggregate: profile, address, credit card as embedded values
subs.legacy_anchor: AddressEJB / ContactInfoEJB / CreditCardEJB / LineItemEJB declared in 4 ejb-jar.xml files (finding #4)
subs.acceptance: Extends the 1.7 stub. One definition each; the EJB 2.0 cross-jar duplication is removed and the before/after is shown in the playback.

subs.title: 4.2 Full URL-protection parity on the 1.8 security chain
subs.acceptance: Extends the 1.8 chain from one protected URL to the whole signon-config.xml set; same URLs protected as the legacy filter, unauthenticated access redirects to sign-in.

subs.title: 4.3 BCrypt password hashing -- LANDED IN 1.8, kept for traceability
subs.acceptance: Closed by 1.8. Kept as a row so the one deliberate deviation from parity keeps its own traceable issue against finding #1 and its README entry.

subs.title: 4.4 Create-account flow + duplicate-account rule
subs.acceptance: Extends the 1.9 registration form with the duplicate-account rule and its screen. Parity test green.

subs.title: 4.5 Customer/profile screens + MessageSource (en_US, ja_JP)
subs.acceptance: Locale switch works; preferredLanguage honoured. ja_JP UI messages are a cut candidate; the locale-scoped DATA model is not.

subs.title: 4.6 Persistence adapters for the customer aggregate
subs.acceptance: Both profiles green.

subs.title: 4.7 REST resource for registration (/api/customers)
subs.legacy_anchor: nothing - grep -rl javax.ws.rs src returns 0 files; kitchensink ships MemberResourceRESTService
subs.acceptance: POST /api/customers registers, GET /api/customers/{id} returns the aggregate, validation failures return 400 with per-field detail. Promotes the tracer-bullet endpoint from 1.9 to the real resource and closes one of the two empty rows in the ADR-0006 mapping table.

epics.title: Persistence strategy & MongoDB stretch goal
epics.summary: Repository ports with two adapters. Built slice by slice, not deferred to the end. See docs/adr/0005-persistence-and-mongodb.md.

subs.title: 7.1 Port/adapter package rules + ArchUnit enforcement
subs.acceptance: Domain imports no Spring Data type.

subs.title: 7.2 Document design: catalog tree vs order aggregate
subs.acceptance: Written up with the removed join and the removed duplication quantified.

subs.title: 7.3 Indexes + text search for catalog
subs.acceptance: Query plans checked, not assumed.

subs.title: 7.4 Profile-switch demo: same suite green under mongo and jpa
subs.acceptance: One command each; results identical. Degrades to Mongo-only if the schedule slips.

subs.title: 7.5 Relational -> document migration note
subs.legacy_anchor: no authoritative DDL for CMP tables (finding #2)
subs.acceptance: Mapping rules and how a real engagement would move the data, not a hand-written script.

epics.title: Delivery: README, demo, playback material
epics.summary: The brief grades the README and the playback as much as the code.

subs.title: 8.1 README with build & run steps
subs.acceptance: A developer with Docker + JDK 21 and no context gets the app running. Explicit requirement of the brief.

subs.title: 8.2 Architecture doc + diagram for the new app
subs.acceptance: Mermaid, same style; side-by-side with the legacy diagrams.

subs.title: 8.3 Demo script: registration slice -> catalog -> profile switch
subs.acceptance: Rehearsed script: register a customer (validation + duplicate rule + BCrypt visible), show the embedded document next to the 4-table CMP graph, browse the catalog, then restart under the jpa profile with the same suite green. Includes the "what was deferred and why" slide from ADR-0006.

subs.title: 8.4 What I learned / how I would run the next one
subs.acceptance: Answers the brief's third playback bullet directly.

subs.title: 8.5 Final gate: clean-clone rehearsal, CI green, gaps listed
subs.acceptance: Fresh git clone -> README steps -> running app, with no undocumented step.
